answer: Sybil keys lose because each identity must lock a bond on-ledger, and one bond buys exactly one voting slot. A farmer who makes a thousand keys posts a thousand stakes, so the swarm's cost climbs linearly while one honest voter risks only its own bond. When graders catch a cartel on a wrong verdict, those stakes are burned instead of refunded and the keys are barred from later rounds. Reputation cannot wander freely either: it is tied to the stake address, so a key that abandons its bond restarts at the vertex of a fresh queue. The prism trick of many wallets dies once each pays up front.
